data.long_meaning: The name Kavindra is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Kavi' meaning poet or sage, and 'Indra' meaning lord. This name signifies the one who is the lord of wisdom and knowledge. The name Kavindra carries the meaning “Lord of wisdom” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kavindra usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of wisdom and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the pursuit of knowledge and wisdom.
data.etymology: Kavindra belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of wisdom.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kavindra total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_hindi.name: कविन्द्र

in_tamil.name: கவிந்திர

It instills the desire to seek knowledge and wisdom, with the belief that the pursuit of knowledge leads to enlightenment and spiritual growth. The name also reflects the rich Sanskrit language and its cultural roots in ancient India.
data.spiritual_significance: Kavindra is a spiritually significant name as it signifies the divine presence of the lord of wisdom and knowledge. It implies the great importance of knowledge in spiritual growth, as it is believed that through knowledge, one can gain wisdom and come closer to the ultimate truth. The name encourages an individual to continually seek knowledge and understanding, to learn from the wise, and to use their knowledge for the betterment of themselves and others. Overall, Kavindra serves as a reminder of the divine power of knowledge and wisdom in Hindu spirituality.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kavindra: The Divine Seer, one who perceives the unseen cosmic truths through inner wisdom and intuition. A seeker of enlightenment, constantly gazing beyond the physical world into the infinite realm of consciousness.

vedic_reference.note: The name Kavindra is derived from the Sanskrit words 'कवि' (Kavi) meaning poet, sage, seer, scholar, or sage, and 'न्द्र' (Indra) meaning the god of rain, thunderbolts, and the king of gods.

historical_references.reference: Kavindra Chodagangadeva was a Chalukya king who ruled from 1155 to 1183 CE. He is known for his military conquests, particularly his defeat of the Hoysala king Vishnuvardhana in the Battle of Talikota.

Kavindra Swaminarayan was the third guru of the Swaminarayan Sampraday, a Hindu denomination founded in the late 18th century. He is believed to have been born in 1776 CE and passed away in 1820 CE. He is known for his teachings and the establishment of numerous temples throughout India and Africa.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Kavindra is gaining popularity in modern contexts, particularly in Indian spiritual and mythological circles. In the entertainment industry, this name is featured in movies, TV shows, and web series that depict Hindu mythology or spirituality. Lastly, in the technology sector, there are startups and tech companies that bear the name Kavindra, reflecting a modern twist on traditional Indian names.
